LESSON: MOMENTS AND EQUILIBRIUM

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: PHYSICS
Strand: Mechanics and Thermal Physics
Topic 1.5: Moments and equilibrium
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 15

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Moments and equilibrium, part of Mechanics and Thermal Physics in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 PHYSICS.

Key inquiry question: How does the stability of bodies affect the designs of their structures?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. Design and carry out activities to determine the position of the centre of gravity of regularly and irregularly shaped objects. Learners with fine motor difficulties could use

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Design and carry out activities to determine the position of the centre of gravity of regularly and irregularly shaped objects. Learners with fine motor difficulties could use

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Moments and equilibrium together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Creativity and Imaginations: The learner develops observation skills as they discover fresh ways of doing things

while carrying out activities to demonstrate torque and couple.

● Citizenship: the learner develops active community life skills as they show responsibility to the community while

carrying out activities to investigate the factors that affect stability of objects.

● Communication and collaboration; as the learner discusses with peers in a group the meaning of centre of gravity and

its significance in day-to-day life.

26

● Critical thinking and problem solving; as the learner solved numerical problems involving centre of gravity, moments

and resolution of forces.

● Learning to learn; as the learner discusses with peers the applications of torque and couples in day-to-day life.

● Digital literacy; as the learner uses digital devices to search for information on factors affecting stability of objects.

Values

● Unity: as the learner shows fairness by displaying team spirit while designing and carrying out activities to determine

the position of centre of gravity of regular and irregular objects.

● Integrity: the learner practices virtue of honesty while presenting genuine results as they design and carry out

activities to determine the position of centre of gravity of regular and irregular objects.

● Love as learners share materials while performing experiments.

● Respect as learners acknowledge the contribution of every member in group discussion.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

● Socio-economic and environmental issues: the learner develops safety and security skills as they become conscious

of road safety while carrying out activities to investigate the factors that affect stability of objects.

● Social cohesion and racial relationships as the learner accommodate other opinions from diverse social and ethnic

backgrounds as they discuss with peers in a group the resolution of forces in mutually perpendicular directions and

their applications.

● Disaster Risk Reduction as the learner observes safety while performing experiments to verify the principle of

moments.

Core competencies to be developed


  -  Communication and collaboration: the learner develops the ability of team members to work well together in every

situation and empathize with each other as they recognize the value of others’ ideas while discussing with peers and

explaining the meaning of the terms used in Physics.


  -  Critical thinking and problem solving: the learner develops the evaluation and decision making skill while they

explore complex problems by identifying when there are no technical solutions as they solve problems involving

energy, work done, power and machines in day-to-day life (velocity ratio, mechanical advantage & efficienc
y) .

Values


  -  Love: the learner shares information with others by portraying a caring attitude while working with others to

construct simple machines.


  -  Responsibility: as the learner shows accountability by caring for own property and those of others while performing

experiments to demonstrate mechanical energy transformations and forms of potential energy.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues (PCI
s) :

Life skills and values education

33


  -  Socio-Economic and Environmental education: the learner appreciates environment and technology as they use

technology in managing the environment while performing experiments to demonstrate mechanical energy

transformations and forms of potential energy.


  -  General history of Africa: as the learner appreciates the development of machines from simple to complex machines

/ evolution of machines from archaic to modern (e.g. steam engine to electric engine
s) .
